message.reasoning:
We have to decide post-turn action. Player p1 (Alpha) has cash 155, holdings: Reading Railroad, Electric Company, and three orange properties (St James Place, Tennessee Avenue, New York Avenue) each with 2 houses. No hotels. Bank has houses remaining 18, hotels 12. Buildable spaces are those three orange properties. They have 2 houses each; building a third house costs? In Monopoly, each house on orange costs $100? Actually orange set: St. James Place $180, Tennessee $180, New York $200. House cost is $100 for each property in orange set. So building a third house on each would cost $100 each, total $300, which exceeds cash 155. Could build one house on one property (cost $100) leaving $55. Could also mortgage Electric Company (value? Electric Company mortgage value is $75? Actually utility mortgage value is $75). Reading Railroad mortgage value is $100. Mortgaging would give cash. Mortgageable spaces: Electric Company and Reading Railroad. Mortgaging gives cash, but also makes them unavailable for rent. Might be good to get cash to build houses or avoid bankruptcy. Cash 155, maybe mortgage Electric Company for $75, cash becomes 230, then can build houses. But building houses costs $100 each. Could build two houses (maybe on two properties) costing $200, leaving $30. Could also build one house on each of two properties costing $200, leaving $30. Could also build one house on each of three properties costing $300, not enough even after mortgage. Could mortgage both to get $175 (75+100) making cash 330, then could build three houses (cost $300) leaving $30. That would bring each orange property to 3 houses, increasing rent. That seems beneficial. However, we must consider that building houses reduces bank houses remaining. Bank has 18 houses, we would use 3 houses (one each). That's fine.

But we can only take one post-turn action at a time. Options: build_houses_or_hotel, mortgage_property, end_turn. We can only do one now. So we need to decide best immediate action. Since we have cash 155, we could either mortgage one property now, then next turn we could build houses. But we could also build a house now using cash 155 (cost $100) on one of the orange properties, leaving $55. That improves rent on that property. Might be good. Mortgaging gives cash but reduces future rent from that property. Which is better? The orange set is already owned, building houses yields high rent. Mortgaging a railroad or utility yields cash but they are not part of a set, and rent is low. Probably better to build a house now, as we have cash. So choose build_houses_or_hotel on one of the orange properties. Which one? All same cost and rent increase. Could pick the one with highest base rent: New York Avenue has higher rent. So build a third house on New York Avenue.

Thus we call build_houses_or_hotel with build_plan: count 1, kind HOUSE, space_key "NEW_YORK_AVENUE". Private thought: reasoning. Public message: maybe say nothing or a friendly comment. Could say "Building a house on New York Avenue." That's fine.

Make tool call.
